scores.evidence: Phase 1 "Ledger schema and tenancy model hardening"; Phase 2 "Depends on: Phase 1; V1 passes"
scores.rationale: Mostly substrate-upward with explicit dependency map and gates, but some ordering flaws (backup/audit in Phase 2 after ledger, V1 benchmark starts after schema, V2 100K-tenant batch test precedes PCI/Stripe) and inconsistencies like Phase 0 using tenancy before Phase 1 hardening.

scores.evidence: "Deploy to staging via CI pipeline (git push → container build → database migration → helm install)."
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real end-to-end slice with CI, rollback and alert, but it runs in staging on internal IP with mocks and no auth, not production.

scores.evidence: "Strong ACID ... | Flip condition: V1 fails and writes/s exceeds limits: move to sharded primaries with quorum commit"
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions are tabulated with reversibility, default, assumption, validation, and flip condition.

scores.evidence: "Design and migrate schema ... Add Postgres RLS policy" before provisioning and posting rules
scores.rationale: Within phases wide-impact items (schema, RLS, backup) come first in places, but ordering is not explicitly reasoned and later phases mix leaf work like onboarding checklist with wide work.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: "Test tenant only; no production credentials; mock Stripe; API endpoint behind allow-list (internal IP)."
scores.rationale: Cross-cutting table gives concrete security content in every phase from Phase 0, though Phase 0 has no auth.

scores.evidence: "Observability (logs, metrics, trace): every API call, ledger posting, invoice state transition, and error logged with tenant_id"
scores.rationale: Observability is concrete in Phase 0 and every subsequent phase.

scores.evidence: "CI builds container with pinned Dockerfile base image; helm chart version tagged; DB migrations versioned."
scores.rationale: Reproducibility has concrete per-phase treatment from Phase 0 through 5.

scores.evidence: "Payment capture failures are retried 3× with exponential backoff; webhook failures are re-queued; circuit breaker on Stripe API rate limits."
scores.rationale: Resilience (rollback, backup, idempotency, retries, kill-switch, failback) appears in every phase with specifics.
Plan explicitly declares AI layer not applicable and adds no AI components.

scores.evidence: "Micro-services refactor ... Condition: Phase 4 monolith throughput or on-call complexity exceeds team budget (on-call incidents > 2/week OR services to run > 5)."
scores.rationale: Deferred items are listed with concrete pull-forward conditions.

note: Strong, thorough plan with concrete gates and threaded cross-cutting concerns; weaknesses are a staging-only skeleton and some ordering inconsistencies.
